label: Diagram 12
caption: Diagram 12 UK zones for exposure to driving rain
description: Diagram 12 is titled "UK zones for exposure to driving rain" and shows a map of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, with two small inset maps in the upper right corner; the upper one is labelled Lerwick and the lower shows a group of smaller islands without a clear label. The upper left contains a legend headed "Exposure zones" beside a column headed "Approximate wind-driven rain* (litres/m² per spell)". Four squares, from white to dark grey, are listed: 1 Sheltered, Less than 33; 2 Moderate, 33 to less than 56.5; 3 Severe, 56.5 to less than 100; 4 Very severe, 100 or more. A footnote reads "*Maximum wall spell index derived from BS 8104". The land areas are shaded in these four tones; generally the darker grey tones sit along the western and northern coasts and the white, sheltered tone lies over the east and south-east of England. Numerous towns are marked by black dots with printed names, for example London, Manchester, Edinburgh, Cardiff and Plymouth.
